sn47.10:4.1: “This morning, sir, I robed up and, taking my bowl and robe, went to the nuns’ quarters, and sat down on the seat spread out.
sn47.10:4.2: Then several nuns came up to me; on arriving, they bowed to me and sat down to one side. Once seated to one side, sir, those nuns said to me:
sn47.10:4.3: ‘Honorable Ānanda, several nuns meditate with their minds firmly established in the four kinds of mindfulness meditation. They have realized a higher distinction than they had before.’
sn47.10:4.4: Having been spoken to this way, sir, those nuns said this:
sn47.10:4.5: ‘That’s how it is, sisters! That’s how it is, sisters!
sn47.10:4.6: Any monk or nun who meditates with their mind firmly established in the four kinds of mindfulness meditation can expect to realize a higher distinction than they had before.’”
